text: So, just to kick things off, could you walk me through your background, and what's brought you over to Australia?
rephrase: Tell me about yourself. What is your experience, and why did you come to Australia?
gist: Tell me about your background and why you came to Australia.
distractors: Tell me about your plans for the next five years in Australia.
Explain why you left your last job.
sampleAnswer: Sure. I'm a [your role] with [number] years of experience, mostly in [industry]. In my last job I [one key achievement]. We moved to Australia because we wanted a stable future for our family, and I'm keen to build my career here.

text: Tell us a bit about yourself. What's your story?
rephrase: Tell me about yourself.
gist: Tell me about yourself.
distractors: Tell me a story about your last project.
What do you do in your free time?

phrases.meaning: tell me about your life and career
phrases.translationRu: расскажи о себе, о жизни и карьере

sampleAnswer: I'm a [your role] with [number] years of experience. I enjoy [what you like about your work], and I'm known for being reliable and detail-oriented. Outside work I like [a hobby]. I recently moved to Australia and I'm looking for a team where I can grow.

text: So what's got you interested in this role, out of all the ones going around at the moment?
rephrase: Why are you interested in this job, when there are many other jobs available?
gist: Why do you want this particular job?
distractors: Which other jobs have you applied for?
What do you know about our company?
sampleAnswer: Three things caught my eye. The role matches my experience in [skill], your company works on [product or mission] that I find interesting, and the job ad mentioned [something from the ad], which is exactly what I enjoy doing.

text: What do you know about us as a company, if anything?
rephrase: What do you know about our company?
gist: What do you know about our company?
distractors: Have you used our product before?
Do you know anyone who works here?

phrases.meaning: it's okay if you know nothing

sampleAnswer: I had a good look at your website and LinkedIn. I know you [what the company does] and that you recently [news or product launch]. I also liked what you say about [a value or culture point], it fits how I like to work.

text: How'd you go settling in? Have you been here long?
rephrase: How is life in Australia so far? How long have you been here?
gist: How long have you been in Australia, and how is it going?
distractors: Where do you plan to live?
Do you have family here?

phrases.translationRu: как прошло, как дела с этим

phrases.meaning: getting used to a new place

sampleAnswer: Pretty well, thanks. I've been here for [time]. There's a lot to get used to, but people have been really friendly. I've sorted out the basics like housing and a bank account, so now I'm focused on finding the right job.

text: Where do you see yourself in, say, three to five years' time?
rephrase: What are your career goals for the next three to five years?
gist: What are your career goals for the next few years?
distractors: How long did you stay in your last three jobs?
When will you be ready to start?
sampleAnswer: I'd like to grow into a more senior [role] and take on more responsibility, for example [mentoring others or leading a project]. Most of all I want to be in a team where I keep learning, and I hope that team could be yours.

text: Give us the quick rundown of your current role. What does a typical day look like?
rephrase: Briefly describe your current job. What do you do on a normal day?
gist: Describe your current job and a normal workday.
distractors: How many hours do you work each day?
What would your ideal job look like?

phrases.meaning: give me (Australians often say us for me)

sampleAnswer: I work as a [role] in a team of [number] people. A typical day starts with a short stand-up meeting. Then I [main task], I [second task], and I work closely with [who you work with]. At the end of the day I update the team on my progress.

text: What would your old manager say is your biggest strength?
rephrase: What would your previous boss say you are best at?
gist: What would your last manager say you do best?
distractors: Why did you leave your old manager?
What is your manager's biggest strength?
sampleAnswer: My old manager would say I'm very reliable. When I take on a task, I finish it properly and on time. For example, [short example]. People knew they could count on me.

text: And what's something you're still working on, professionally speaking?
rephrase: What is a weakness you are trying to improve at work?
gist: What work skill are you still trying to improve?
distractors: What project are you working on right now?
What do you do outside work?
sampleAnswer: I'm working on [a real skill to improve, for example public speaking or saying no to extra work]. To improve it, I [what you are doing about it], and I can already see progress. For example, [small result].

text: What made you want to get into this line of work in the first place?
rephrase: Why did you choose this career?
gist: Why did you choose this career?
distractors: When did you first start working?
Would you like to change careers?
sampleAnswer: I've always liked [what attracts you to this work]. When I first tried [first experience], I really enjoyed it, and I've kept growing in this field ever since. I like that my work [the impact your work has].

text: Is there anything on your resume you reckon we should dig into a bit more?
rephrase: Is there something on your CV you want to talk about in more detail?
gist: What part of your CV should we discuss in more detail?
distractors: Can you send us your resume again?
Is there a mistake on your resume?
sampleAnswer: I'd be happy to talk more about my time at [company]. That's where I [main achievement], and I think it's the most relevant to this role. I can walk you through what I did and the results.

text: How do you like to unwind outside of work?
rephrase: What do you do to relax after work?
gist: What do you do to relax outside work?
distractors: Do you often work late?
How do you get to work?
sampleAnswer: I like to keep active. I go for walks or to the beach, and on weekends I spend time with my family. I also enjoy [a hobby]. It helps me switch off and come back to work fresh.

text: What sort of team do you work best in? Big, small, a bit of both?
rephrase: What kind of team do you prefer?
gist: What size and type of team suits you best?
distractors: How many people did you manage?
Who was the best person in your team?
sampleAnswer: I've worked in both, and I'm happy in either. In smaller teams I like that everyone talks to each other directly. In bigger teams I like learning from more people. What matters most to me is open communication and helping each other.

text: Have you had any experience working with Aussie companies before, or would this be your first?
rephrase: Have you worked for an Australian company before?
gist: Have you worked for an Australian company before?
distractors: Is this your first job?
Have you visited Australia before?
sampleAnswer: This would be my first Australian company, but I've worked with international teams and clients before, so I'm used to different working styles. I'm a quick learner and I'm looking forward to it.

text: Before we get stuck into it, how's your day been so far?
rephrase: Before we start, how is your day going?
gist: Small talk: how is your day going?
distractors: Are you ready to start work today?
Did you find our office easily?
sampleAnswer: Good, thanks! It's been a busy morning, but I'm glad to be here. How's your day going?

text: Can you tell me about a time you tracked down a really tricky bug? And how did you go about raising it with the devs?
rephrase: Tell me about a difficult bug you found. How did you investigate it, and how did you tell the developers?
gist: Describe a hard bug you found, and how you reported it to developers.
distractors: Describe a bug that a developer found in your tests.
Explain how you would train new developers.

phrases.translationRu: как именно ты об этом сообщил

sampleAnswer: Yes. We had a bug that only happened sometimes, for example [describe it]. I collected logs, found the exact steps, and noticed it only happened when [the condition]. I wrote a clear bug report with steps, logs and a screenshot, and walked the developer through it. It was fixed in [time].

text: Righto, last one from me. If a developer pushes back and reckons your bug isn't really a bug, how do you handle that?
rephrase: Last question. If a developer says your bug is not a real bug, what do you do?
gist: What do you do when a developer says your bug is not a real bug?
distractors: What do you do when you cannot reproduce a bug?
What was the last bug you reported?
sampleAnswer: First I make sure I understand their point. Then I show the facts: the steps, the expected result from the requirements, and the impact on users. If we still disagree, I ask the product owner to decide. It's not about who is right, it's about the user.

text: The team's spread across a few time zones, so there isn't a heap of overlap. How would you keep everyone on the same page?
rephrase: The team works in different time zones. How would you keep communication clear?
gist: How would you keep a team in different time zones informed?
distractors: Are you happy to work night shifts?
How many people were in your last team?
sampleAnswer: I'd write things down. Clear updates in the team chat, notes after each meeting, and status in the tickets, so people can catch up when they start their day. I'd also use the overlap hours for the most important conversations.

text: Tell me about a time you had to work to a really tight deadline. How'd you go?
rephrase: Describe a time you had very little time to finish work. How did it go?
gist: Tell me about working to a very short deadline and the result.
distractors: How do you plan your work for the week?
Have you ever missed a deadline on purpose?

phrases.translationRu: как прошло, как дела с этим

sampleAnswer: We once had only [time] to test a release. I agreed with the team on the most important features, focused on those first, and gave daily updates on risks. We released on time and there were no critical issues in production.

text: Can you think of a time you stuffed something up at work? What happened, and what did you learn?
rephrase: Tell me about a mistake you made at work and what you learned.
gist: Describe a mistake you made at work and what you learned.
distractors: Tell me about a mistake your colleague made.
How do you check your work for mistakes?

phrases.phrase: can you think of a time

sampleAnswer: Once I [the mistake]. As soon as I noticed, I told my manager, fixed the problem, and checked nothing else was affected. Since then I always [what you do differently now]. It taught me that it's better to raise a problem early.

text: Walk me through a time you had to deal with a difficult stakeholder.
rephrase: Tell me step by step about a time you worked with a difficult person, like a manager or client.
gist: Describe working with a difficult manager or client.
distractors: Who are the stakeholders in your current project?
How do you deal with stress?

phrases.meaning: a person who cares about the result: client, manager, product owner

sampleAnswer: A client kept changing the requirements late in the project. I set up a short weekly call, wrote down every agreement, and showed how each change affected the deadline. After that the requests became more realistic and our relationship improved.

text: Have you ever had to juggle a few competing priorities? How did you decide what to tackle first?
rephrase: Have you had many important tasks at once? How did you choose what to do first?
gist: How do you choose what to do first when several tasks are urgent?
distractors: Do you like to work on many projects at once?
Which task do you enjoy the most?
sampleAnswer: Yes. I look at the impact and the deadline of each task. If it's not clear, I ask my manager which one matters most for the business. Then I tell the people whose tasks will wait, so nobody is surprised.

text: Tell me about a time you went above and beyond for a customer or your team.
rephrase: Tell me about a time you did more than you had to.
gist: Describe a time you did more than was expected.
distractors: How many hours a week do you usually work?
Tell me about your best customer.
sampleAnswer: A customer had a problem late on a Friday that blocked their work. It wasn't my task, but I stayed, found the cause together with a developer, and they could work again the same evening. They later thanked our team in writing.

text: Give me an example of when you disagreed with your manager. How did you handle it?
rephrase: Tell me about a disagreement with your manager. What did you do?
gist: Describe a disagreement with your manager and how you handled it.
distractors: Why did you change managers?
What do you like about your manager?
sampleAnswer: My manager wanted to [their plan], but I thought it was risky because [reason]. I asked for a short meeting and showed my data. We agreed on [the compromise]. Even when I disagree, I respect the final decision.

text: How do you go about getting up to speed on something you know nothing about?
rephrase: How do you learn something completely new?
gist: How do you learn a new topic quickly?
distractors: How do you explain something new to others?
What new technology do you want to learn?
sampleAnswer: I start with the official documentation and ask colleagues for a short overview. Then I try it hands-on on a small example. I write notes as I go, and I'm not afraid to ask questions early.

text: Tell me about a time things didn't go to plan on a project. What did you do?
rephrase: Tell me about a project problem and how you reacted.
gist: Describe a project that went wrong and what you did.
distractors: How do you plan a new project?
Tell me about your favourite project.
sampleAnswer: On one project a key system wasn't ready in time. I told the team about the risk early, we changed the plan and tested with [a workaround], and we still delivered the most important part on time. The rest came in the next release.

text: Have you ever had to give a colleague some tough feedback? How'd you approach that?
rephrase: Did you ever have to tell a coworker something negative about their work? How did you do it?
gist: How did you give difficult feedback to a colleague?
distractors: How do you react to negative feedback?
How often do you have team meetings?
sampleAnswer: Yes. I did it in private, focused on the work and not the person, and gave a specific example. I also offered to help. My colleague took it well, and the problem didn't happen again.

text: What's an achievement you're really proud of, and why does it stand out for you?
rephrase: What is your proudest achievement, and why is it special for you?
gist: What achievement are you most proud of, and why?
distractors: What award did your company win?
Why do you want to stand out in the team?

phrases.meaning: be special, different from the rest

sampleAnswer: I'm proud of [achievement]. Before that, [the problem]. I [what you did], and as a result [measurable result]. It stands out because it helped the whole team, not just me.

text: Say you've got a heap on your plate and your manager drops another urgent task on you. What do you do?
rephrase: You are already very busy and your manager gives you another urgent task. What do you do?
gist: What do you do when you are very busy and get another urgent task?
distractors: How do you ask your manager for more work?
What do you do when there's no work?
sampleAnswer: I'd talk to my manager straight away. I'd show what I'm working on and ask which task is the priority now. Then I'd tell anyone affected that their task might move. That way nothing important gets dropped quietly.

text: Tell me about a time you had to explain something technical to someone who wasn't across the details.
rephrase: Tell me about explaining a technical topic to a non-technical person.
gist: Describe explaining something technical to a non-technical person.
distractors: Tell me about a technical course you took.
How do you write technical documentation?
sampleAnswer: I had to explain a technical problem to [a manager or client]. I avoided jargon, used a simple comparison, and focused on what it meant for them: the risk, the impact on users, and what we planned to do. They understood and approved the plan.

text: What are you looking for, salary wise? And just to be clear, is that base, or are we talking package, including super?
rephrase: What salary do you expect? Is that without superannuation, or including it?
gist: What salary do you expect, and does it include super?
distractors: How much did you earn in your last job?
Do you need visa sponsorship?

phrases.meaning: salary plus super and other benefits
phrases.translationRu: пакет: оклад плюс super и бонусы

sampleAnswer: I'm looking for around [amount] base, plus super. I'm a bit flexible depending on the whole package, for example training or flexible hours. What's the range for this role?

text: And what's your availability like? What sort of notice period are we looking at?
rephrase: When can you start? Do you need to give notice to your current employer?
gist: When can you start, and what is your notice period?
distractors: Which days of the week are you free for an interview?
How long did you stay in your last job?

phrases.meaning: when you are free to start
time you must work after you resign

phrases.phrase: what sort of... are we looking at

sampleAnswer: I'm available to start [date or 'straight away']. [If you have a job: My notice period is (number) weeks.] I'm happy to do any paperwork or onboarding before that.

text: Are you after full-time, part-time, or are you open to contract work?
rephrase: Do you want full-time, part-time, or contract work?
gist: What type of employment do you want?
distractors: How many hours did you work last week?
Do you have a contract with your current employer?
sampleAnswer: I'm mainly after a full-time permanent role, but I'm open to a contract if it's the right fit.

text: Do you have full working rights in Australia?
rephrase: Are you allowed to work in Australia without limits?
gist: Are you legally allowed to work in Australia?
distractors: Do you have a driver's licence?
Have you worked in Australia before?
sampleAnswer: Yes, I have full working rights in Australia. [Or: I'm on a (visa) visa that allows me to work full-time.] I can provide the details whenever you need them.

text: How would you feel about coming into the office a couple of days a week?
rephrase: Are you okay working in the office two days a week?
gist: Are you okay with working in the office two days a week?
distractors: How long does it take you to get to the office?
Would you like to work from home full-time?
sampleAnswer: That works for me. I like having some time with the team in person, and I'm comfortable working from home on the other days.

text: Are you okay with the occasional bit of after-hours work around releases?
rephrase: Can you sometimes work in the evening when there is a release?
gist: Can you sometimes work after hours during releases?
distractors: How often do you release software?
Do you want overtime pay?
sampleAnswer: Yes, that's fine. I understand releases sometimes need extra time. As long as it's planned in advance when possible, I'm happy to help.

text: We'd be looking at a probation period of six months. Is that alright with you?
rephrase: The first six months are a trial period. Is that okay?
gist: Do you accept a six-month probation period?
distractors: Can you start in six months?
Did you have probation in your last job?

phrases.meaning: trial period at the start of a job

sampleAnswer: Yes, that's completely fine. I understand it's standard in Australia, and it's a good chance for both of us to make sure it's the right fit.

text: Have you got any holidays booked in the next few months that we should know about?
rephrase: Do you have any planned holidays soon?
gist: Do you have any planned holidays soon?
distractors: How many holidays do you want per year?
Where did you go on your last holiday?
sampleAnswer: No, nothing booked at the moment. [Or: I have a short trip in (month), but I'm happy to talk about it.]

text: Just so you know, the budget for this role sits around ninety to a hundred K plus super. Does that work for you?
rephrase: The salary is about 90 to 100 thousand dollars plus super. Is that okay?
gist: Is a salary of 90 to 100 thousand plus super okay for you?
distractors: How much super did you get in your last job?
Can you work for 90 to 100 days?
sampleAnswer: Thanks for letting me know. That range works for me, especially with super on top. I'd love to hear more about the other parts of the package too.

text: Would you need any sponsorship, now or down the track?
rephrase: Will you need visa sponsorship now or in the future?
gist: Will you need visa sponsorship now or later?
distractors: Do you need help moving to a new city?
Who will sponsor this project?
sampleAnswer: No, I don't need sponsorship. [Or: Yes, I would need sponsorship. My current visa allows me to work until (date).]

text: Are you currently interviewing anywhere else?
rephrase: Do you have interviews with other companies now?
gist: Are you interviewing with other companies?
distractors: Have you interviewed people before?
Where else have you worked?
sampleAnswer: Yes, I'm talking to a couple of other companies, but this role is one of my top choices because [reason].

text: If we made you an offer, how soon could you kick off?
rephrase: If we offer you the job, when can you start?
gist: How soon can you start if you get an offer?
distractors: What offer would you accept?
How soon can you finish this interview?
sampleAnswer: I could start [date or 'within two weeks']. If you need someone sooner, I'll do my best to make it work.

text: Are you happy for us to reach out to a couple of your referees?
rephrase: Can we contact some of your references?
gist: Can we contact your references?
distractors: Can you send us a few work examples?
Can you refer a friend for this job?

phrases.meaning: people who give you a reference

sampleAnswer: Yes, of course. I can send you the contact details of [number] referees today.

text: Whereabouts are you based? Is the commute going to be a problem?
rephrase: Where do you live? Will travelling to the office be difficult?
gist: Where do you live, and is travel to the office a problem?
distractors: Where were you born?
Do you have a car?

phrases.meaning: the trip to work and back

sampleAnswer: I live in [suburb]. It's about [time] to the office by [car or public transport], so the commute is fine.

text: Just to manage expectations, the next step would be a technical chat with the team. That suit you?
rephrase: The next stage is a technical interview with the team. Is that okay?
gist: Are you okay with a technical interview as the next step?
distractors: Can you manage the team's expectations?
Would you like to chat with the team at lunch?

phrases.meaning: an informal talk, often an interview

sampleAnswer: Yes, that suits me. Is there anything I should prepare for the technical chat?

text: Have you had much exposure to mocking in your test setup? And how do you make sure your automated tests are actually reliable, and not flaky?
rephrase: Do you use mocks in your tests? And how do you make your automated tests stable?
gist: Have you used mocks, and how do you keep automated tests stable?
distractors: How many automated tests have you written?
Which test framework do you like the most?
sampleAnswer: Yes. I use mocks to isolate the parts I'm testing, for example a mock server for API responses. To keep tests reliable, I use stable test data, wait for elements instead of fixed delays, and run each test independently. When a test is flaky, I find the root cause instead of just re-running it.

text: Fair enough. Have you had a crack at testing anything A.I. driven, like L.L.M. features, or agents? No worries if not.
rephrase: Have you tested any AI features, for example LLMs or AI agents? It's okay if you haven't.
gist: Have you tested AI features like LLMs or agents?
distractors: Do you use AI tools to write your tests?
What do you think about AI replacing testers?
sampleAnswer: Yes. I tested [chatbot or AI feature] built on [the model or API]. I created test questions with expected answers and checked the replies for accuracy, hallucinations and tone. I re-ran the set every time the prompt or model changed. [If not: Not yet, but I've been learning about it, and I'd love to.]

text: How would you go about testing a login screen if we gave you, say, twenty minutes?
rephrase: How would you test a login screen in twenty minutes?
gist: How would you test a login screen in a short time?
distractors: How long does it take you to log in?
Have you ever designed a login screen?
sampleAnswer: First the happy path: a valid login works. Then the main negative cases: wrong password, empty fields, a locked account. After that, quick checks of security and usability: the password is hidden, there's a limit on attempts, error messages don't reveal too much. I'd note anything I didn't have time for.

text: Where do you sit on the whole manual versus automation debate?
rephrase: What is your opinion about manual testing compared to automation?
gist: What do you think about manual versus automated testing?
distractors: How many manual testers were in your last team?
Which automation tool is the most popular?
sampleAnswer: I think we need both. Automation is great for stable, repeated checks like regression. Manual and exploratory testing is better for new features and for things that need a human eye, like usability.

text: How do you decide what's worth automating and what's not?
rephrase: How do you choose which tests to automate?
gist: How do you choose which tests to automate?
distractors: How long does it take to automate a test?
Which tests have you deleted?
sampleAnswer: I automate tests that run often, are stable, and protect important flows, like login or payments. I don't automate features that change every week or checks that are cheaper to do by hand once.

text: Talk me through how you'd write up a bug so a dev can pick it up straight away.
rephrase: How do you write a bug report so a developer understands it immediately?
gist: How do you write a clear bug report?
distractors: How do you pick which bugs to fix first?
How fast do developers fix your bugs?
sampleAnswer: A short, clear title. Exact steps to reproduce, expected and actual result, environment and app version. Then screenshots, a video or logs, and the impact and severity. A developer should be able to reproduce it without asking me anything.

text: What's your take on testing in production? Ever done it?
rephrase: What do you think about testing on the live system? Have you done it?
gist: What do you think about testing in production?
distractors: Have you ever caused a production incident?
How often do you release to production?

phrases.meaning: on the live system real users use

sampleAnswer: It can be useful, carefully. For example smoke tests after a release, or monitoring and feature flags. I've done [what you did, for example post-release smoke checks]. It never replaces testing before release.

text: How do you get your head around a new codebase or product quickly?
rephrase: How do you understand a new product or code quickly?
gist: How do you learn a new product or codebase quickly?
distractors: How do you write code faster?
Which products do you use every day?
sampleAnswer: I start by using the product like a real user. Then I read the docs and the existing tests, look at the main flows, and ask a developer for a quick walkthrough. I also look at recent bugs to see where the weak spots are.

text: Have you worked much with APIs? What tools do you reach for?
rephrase: Do you have experience testing APIs? Which tools do you use?
gist: What is your API testing experience, and which tools do you use?
distractors: Have you designed an API yourself?
Which tools does your team need?
sampleAnswer: Yes, a lot. I use [Postman or a similar tool] for manual API testing and [REST Assured or a similar library] for automated tests. I check status codes, the response body, error handling and the API contract.

text: How do you fit into a CI pipeline? Like, where do your tests actually run?
rephrase: How do your tests work in CI? Where are they executed?
gist: Where and how do your automated tests run in CI?
distractors: How do you build the pipeline for developers?
How long have you used CI?
sampleAnswer: My tests run in [CI tool] on every merge request. Fast tests run on every change, the full regression runs [nightly or before release]. If a test fails, the merge is blocked and the team gets the report.

text: If you only had half a day for regression before a release, what would you focus on?
rephrase: You have four hours for regression testing before release. What do you test?
gist: What would you test with very little regression time?
distractors: How long does your regression usually take?
Would you delay the release by half a day?
sampleAnswer: I'd focus on the riskiest areas: the main user flows, anything that changed in this release, and the areas with recent bugs. I'd tell the team clearly what I didn't test, so they can decide on the risk.

text: How do you deal with a test that passes on your machine but keeps falling over in the pipeline?
rephrase: A test passes locally but fails in CI. What do you do?
gist: What do you do when a test passes locally but fails in CI?
distractors: How do you set up your local machine?
How do you deal with a broken laptop?
sampleAnswer: Usually it's a difference in the environment, timing or test data. I'd compare the CI logs and settings with my machine, check for race conditions and shared data, and try to reproduce it in a similar environment. Then I fix the root cause.

text: Have you had a go at performance or load testing at all?
rephrase: Have you tried performance or load testing?
gist: Do you have performance or load testing experience?
distractors: How do you improve your own performance at work?
How much load can you handle at work?
sampleAnswer: A bit. I've used [tool, for example JMeter or k6] to check response times under load. [If not: Not much yet, but I understand the basics, and I'd be happy to learn.]

text: How do you work out the acceptance criteria when the ticket's a bit thin?
rephrase: How do you find the requirements when a task has little detail?
gist: How do you clarify requirements when a ticket has few details?
distractors: How do you write a ticket for developers?
How do you close tickets faster?

phrases.meaning: conditions that show a task is done

sampleAnswer: I talk to the product owner or the developer early. I write down my understanding as simple examples, like 'given, when, then', and ask them to confirm. That way we agree before anything gets built.

text: What does a good test strategy look like to you, in a nutshell?
rephrase: Briefly, what is a good test strategy?
gist: Briefly describe a good test strategy.
distractors: Who writes the test strategy in your team?
What does your test environment look like?
sampleAnswer: A good test strategy says what we test, how and when, based on risk. Lots of fast unit tests, fewer integration tests and only a few end-to-end tests, all running in CI, plus exploratory testing for new features.

text: So what's got you keen on volunteering with us?
rephrase: Why do you want to volunteer with our organisation?
gist: Why do you want to volunteer with us?
distractors: How many hours did you volunteer last year?
Do you want a paid job with us?
sampleAnswer: I'd like to give something back to the community, and I really like what your organisation does for [the people you help]. I also want to meet people and get to know my new country better.

text: Have you done any volunteering before, back home or here?
rephrase: Do you have any volunteer experience, in your country or in Australia?
gist: Have you volunteered before?
distractors: Where is your home country?
Do you know other volunteers here?

phrases.meaning: in the country you come from

sampleAnswer: Yes. Back home I [what you did, for example helped at a clinic or a charity]. [Or: Not yet, but I've helped friends and neighbours, and now I'd like to do it properly.]

text: How many hours a week could you realistically give us?
rephrase: How many hours a week can you volunteer?
gist: How many hours a week can you volunteer?
distractors: How many hours a week do you work?
When is the best time to call you?
sampleAnswer: Realistically, around [number] hours a week. I'd rather start with what I can do reliably and add more later.

text: Are you right to do weekends, or are you more of a weekday person?
rephrase: Can you volunteer on weekends, or only on weekdays?
gist: Can you volunteer on weekends or only on weekdays?
distractors: What do you usually do on weekends?
Which day do you start work?

phrases.meaning: are you able to, is it okay for you (Australian)
someone who prefers Monday to Friday

sampleAnswer: I can do [weekdays or weekends or both]. My best days are [days].

text: Do you have a current police check, or would you be happy to get one?
rephrase: Do you have a police certificate? If not, can you get one?
gist: Do you have a police check, or can you get one?
distractors: Have you ever called the police?
Do you want to work with the police?

phrases.meaning: a certificate about your criminal record

sampleAnswer: Yes, I have a current police check. [Or: Not yet, but I'm happy to get one straight away.]

text: Some of our roles need a Working With Children Check. Is that something you've got sorted?
rephrase: Some roles need a Working With Children Check. Do you have one?
gist: Do you have a Working With Children Check?
distractors: Do you have children?
Have you worked in a school?

phrases.meaning: a state clearance to work with kids

sampleAnswer: Yes, I have one. [Or: Not yet, but I'll apply for it this week.]

text: How would you handle someone who's really upset or a bit aggro?
rephrase: What would you do if a person is very upset or aggressive?
gist: How do you deal with an upset or aggressive person?
distractors: What makes you upset at work?
How do you handle a lot of work?
sampleAnswer: I'd stay calm, speak slowly and listen. I'd try to understand what's wrong and show that I care. If I felt unsafe, I'd step back and get help from a staff member.

text: You might hear some pretty personal stuff. How do you go with keeping things confidential?
rephrase: People may tell you private things. Can you keep information private?
gist: Can you keep private information confidential?
distractors: Do you like to share personal stories?
How do you store documents?
sampleAnswer: I understand that confidentiality is really important. I wouldn't share anything about clients with anyone outside the team. If I heard something that suggests someone is at risk, I'd tell my supervisor.

text: Tell me about a time you worked as part of a team to help someone out.
rephrase: Give an example of teamwork to help another person.
gist: Describe helping someone as part of a team.
distractors: How big was your last team?
Who helped you when you arrived?
sampleAnswer: At [place], we helped [who] with [what]. I [your part], and the team [what they did]. In the end [the result]. I liked that we all worked together.

text: What skills from your background do you reckon you'd bring to this role?
rephrase: Which of your skills would be useful in this volunteer role?
gist: What skills would you bring to this role?
distractors: What new skills do you want to learn?
What is your educational background?
sampleAnswer: I have experience in [your field, for example medicine], so I'm calm in stressful situations and good at listening to people. I'm also organised and reliable.

text: Our volunteers come from all walks of life. How do you go working with people from different cultures?
rephrase: Our volunteers are very different people. Are you comfortable working with other cultures?
gist: How do you work with people from different cultures?
distractors: Which countries have you visited?
How many languages do you speak?
sampleAnswer: I'm an immigrant myself, so I know how it feels to be new. I'm open, respectful and curious about other cultures, and I always try to listen first.

text: Do you speak any other languages? That can be a real help with some of our clients.
rephrase: Do you speak other languages? It helps with some clients.
gist: Do you speak any other languages?
distractors: Would you like to learn English?
Which language do our clients speak?
sampleAnswer: Yes, I speak [languages]. I'd be happy to help clients who speak them.

text: Volunteering can be pretty full on at times. How do you look after yourself?
rephrase: Volunteering can be stressful. How do you take care of yourself?
gist: How do you manage stress and look after yourself?
distractors: How do you look after your family?
How long is a full shift?
sampleAnswer: I try to keep a good balance: enough sleep, exercise and time with family. If something is hard, I talk to my supervisor or the team.

text: What would you do if a client asked you for something that's outside your role?
rephrase: What if a client asks you to do something that is not your job?
gist: What do you do when a client asks for something outside your role?
distractors: What would you ask a client first?
Which roles do you want to try?
sampleAnswer: I'd explain politely that it's outside my role and I'm not allowed to do it. Then I'd tell my supervisor, so the client gets the right help.

text: And how are you getting here? Have you got your own transport?
rephrase: How will you travel here? Do you have a car?
gist: How will you get here? Do you have transport?
distractors: Where are you going next?
Can you drive our clients?
sampleAnswer: I'll come by [car or public transport]. It's about [time] from my place, so that's no problem.

text: What made you want to get into aged care?
rephrase: Why did you choose aged care work?
gist: Why do you want to work in aged care?
distractors: How old are you?
Do you have older relatives here?
sampleAnswer: I like helping people, and I find it really meaningful to support older people so they can live with dignity. [If true: I have a medical background, so caring for people comes naturally to me.]

text: Have you done your Cert III in Individual Support, or are you working towards it?
rephrase: Do you have the Certificate III in Individual Support, or are you studying for it?
gist: Do you have a Cert III in Individual Support?
distractors: Which certificate do you want to get next?
Can you support other students?

phrases.meaning: Certificate III, the basic aged care qualification
phrases.translationRu: сертификат III, базовая квалификация по уходу

sampleAnswer: Yes, I've completed it. [Or: I'm studying it now and I'll finish in (month). I've already done my placement at (place).]

text: Talk me through how you'd help a resident with a shower while keeping their dignity.
rephrase: How would you help a resident shower and respect their privacy?
gist: How do you help a resident shower with dignity?
distractors: How often should residents shower?
Who cleans the bathrooms?

phrases.meaning: a person living in an aged care home

sampleAnswer: I'd ask for their consent first and explain each step. I'd keep them covered with a towel as much as possible, check the water temperature, and let them do as much as they can themselves. I'd always respect their choices.

text: How would you go with a resident with dementia who's getting agitated and wants to go home?
rephrase: A resident with dementia is upset and wants to go home. What do you do?
gist: How do you calm a resident with dementia who wants to go home?
distractors: Have you studied dementia?
When can residents go home?

phrases.meaning: an illness that causes memory loss

sampleAnswer: I'd stay calm, speak gently and listen. I wouldn't argue. I'd try to redirect them with something they like, for example a cup of tea or a walk. I'd follow their care plan and tell the RN.

text: What would you do if you found a resident on the floor?
rephrase: What would you do if a resident has fallen?
gist: What do you do if a resident has fallen?
distractors: How do you clean the floor safely?
Where do residents sit?
sampleAnswer: I wouldn't move them. I'd stay with them, call for help and tell the registered nurse straight away. Then I'd follow the facility's procedure and write an incident report.

text: How do you go about manual handling? Have you used a hoist before?
rephrase: How do you lift and move people safely? Have you used a lifting machine?
gist: How do you move residents safely, and have you used a hoist?
distractors: How much can you lift?
Have you done physical work before?
sampleAnswer: I always check the care plan first, use the right equipment, and ask for a second person when it's needed. Yes, I've used a hoist [in training or at work]. I never lift a resident on my own if it's not safe.

text: If you noticed a resident had a new bruise, what would you do?
rephrase: You see a new bruise on a resident. What do you do?
gist: What do you do if you notice a new bruise on a resident?
distractors: How do you treat a bruise?
Have you ever had a bad bruise?

phrases.meaning: a dark mark on the skin after a hit

sampleAnswer: I'd tell the registered nurse straight away and write it down in the notes. If I thought it could be abuse, I'd follow the reporting procedure. The resident's safety comes first.

text: What does person-centred care mean to you?
rephrase: What is your understanding of person-centred care?
gist: What is person-centred care?
distractors: Who is the centre of your team?
Why do you care about people?

phrases.meaning: care built around the person's own wishes

sampleAnswer: It means seeing the person, not just the tasks. I respect their choices, their routine and their culture, and I involve them and their family in decisions about their care.

text: We work on a rotating roster, including nights and weekends. Are you right with that?
rephrase: Shifts change, including nights and weekends. Is that okay?
gist: Can you work rotating shifts, including nights and weekends?
distractors: Can you make the roster for the team?
Do you sleep well at night?

phrases.meaning: a shift schedule that keeps changing

sampleAnswer: Yes, I'm fine with that. I understand care is needed around the clock, and I'm flexible.

text: A family member is unhappy with the care their mum's getting and starts having a go at you. How do you handle it?
rephrase: A relative is angry about their mother's care and shouts at you. What do you do?
gist: How do you handle an angry family member?
distractors: How do you talk to your own mother?
When can families visit?
sampleAnswer: I'd stay calm, listen and not take it personally. I'd show that I understand their worry, and tell them I'll pass it on to the registered nurse or manager, who can follow up properly.

text: What would you do if a resident refuses their medication or doesn't want to eat?
rephrase: A resident won't take medicine or won't eat. What do you do?
gist: What do you do when a resident refuses medicine or food?
distractors: Which medicine is the most common?
What do residents like to eat?
sampleAnswer: I wouldn't force them. I'd gently try to find out why, maybe they feel unwell, or they don't like the food. I'd tell the RN and write it in the notes.

text: Can you tell me about a time you supported someone at the end of their life?
rephrase: Have you cared for someone who was dying?
gist: Describe supporting someone at the end of their life.
distractors: What are your plans for later life?
How long do residents usually stay?

phrases.meaning: the last days before death, palliative care

sampleAnswer: Yes. I [your experience]. I focused on keeping the person comfortable and pain-free, I sat with them, and I supported the family. It's hard, but it's a privilege to be there.

text: How do you make sure your notes and handover are up to scratch?
rephrase: How do you keep good records and pass information to the next shift?
gist: How do you write good notes and do a clear handover?
distractors: How do you take notes at school?
Who checks your handwriting?

phrases.meaning: passing information to the next shift

sampleAnswer: I write my notes during or right after care, so I don't forget anything. They're clear, factual and on time. At handover I mention any changes or concerns, and I check the next person understood.

text: Have you got your NDIS Worker Screening and a current police clearance?
rephrase: Do you have NDIS Worker Screening and a police check?
gist: Do you have the required screening and police checks?
distractors: Do you work for the NDIS?
Have you screened other workers?

phrases.meaning: a clearance to work with people with disability
phrases.translationRu: проверка для работы с людьми с инвалидностью

sampleAnswer: Yes, I have both. [Or: I've applied and I'm waiting for the result. I can send you the reference number.]

text: What's your understanding of duty of care?
rephrase: What does duty of care mean?
gist: What is duty of care?
distractors: Who pays for care?
What duties did you have at home?

phrases.meaning: the legal duty to keep people safe

sampleAnswer: Duty of care means I must keep residents safe from harm, while still respecting their choices. If something could hurt them, I need to act and report it.

text: Hi there! What's your name, love?
rephrase: What is your name?
gist: What is your name?
distractors: Where is your mum?
How old are you?

phrases.meaning: a friendly word adults say to kids (Australian)

sampleAnswer: Hi! My name is [your name].

text: And how old are you, mate?
rephrase: How old are you?
gist: How old are you?
distractors: What class are you in?
What is your friend's name?
sampleAnswer: I'm [ten] years old.

text: Where are you from? Have you just moved here?
rephrase: Which country are you from? Are you new here?
gist: Where are you from, and are you new here?
distractors: Where do you live now?
Do you like moving house?
sampleAnswer: I'm from [your country]. Yes, we just moved here.

translationRu.text: Откуда ты? Ты только что переехала сюда?
translationRu.sampleAnswer: Я из [твоя страна]. Да, мы только что переехали.

text: Do you need to go to the toilet? Just put your hand up and ask.
rephrase: If you need the toilet, raise your hand and ask.
gist: Raise your hand and ask to go to the toilet.
distractors: Wash your hands after lunch.
Put your bag on the hook.
sampleAnswer: Excuse me, Miss. Can I go to the toilet, please?

translationRu.text: Тебе нужно в туалет? Просто подними руку и спроси.
translationRu.sampleAnswer: Извините, мисс. Можно мне в туалет, пожалуйста?

text: Righto, everyone, grab your hats. No hat, no play!
rephrase: Everyone, take your hats. You can't play outside without a hat.
gist: Take your hat. You need it to play outside.
distractors: Put your hats in your bags.
We are not playing today.

phrases.meaning: a school sun rule: no hat means no playing outside

sampleAnswer: Okay! I've got my hat.

translationRu.text: Так, все, берите панамы. Без панамы гулять нельзя!

text: It's recess now. Have you got something to eat?
rephrase: It is the short break now. Do you have food?
gist: Do you have a snack for the break?
distractors: Is your lunch hot?
Do you want to go home?

phrases.meaning: the short break in the morning

sampleAnswer: Yes, I have a snack in my bag.

translationRu.text: Сейчас перемена. У тебя есть что поесть?
translationRu.sampleAnswer: Да, у меня в рюкзаке перекус.

text: Did you bring your water bottle? You can fill it up at the bubbler.
rephrase: Do you have a water bottle? You can get water at the drinking fountain.
gist: Do you have a water bottle to fill up?
distractors: Do you want a new bottle?
Is the water too cold?
sampleAnswer: Yes, here it is. Where is the bubbler?

translationRu.text: Ты взяла бутылку для воды? Можно набрать воду в фонтанчике.

text: Can you pop your bag on the hook and come sit on the mat?
rephrase: Put your bag on the hook and sit on the mat.
gist: Put your bag away and sit on the mat.
distractors: Bring your bag to the mat.
Take your bag home.

phrases.meaning: the carpet where the class sits together

sampleAnswer: Okay! Where do I sit?

translationRu.text: Повесь рюкзак на крючок и садись на коврик.

text: Do you want to play with us at lunch? We're playing handball.
rephrase: Do you want to play handball with us at lunchtime?
gist: Do you want to play with us at lunch?
distractors: Do you want to eat lunch with us?
Can you buy us lunch?

phrases.meaning: a popular school game with a ball and four squares
phrases.translationRu: хэндбол, игра с мячом в квадратах

sampleAnswer: Yes, please! Can you show me the rules?

translationRu.text: Хочешь поиграть с нами на большой перемене? Мы играем в хэндбол.

text: What's your favourite subject so far?
rephrase: Which school subject do you like the most?
gist: What subject do you like best?
distractors: What is your favourite food?
How far is your school?

phrases.meaning: maths, art, sport and so on

sampleAnswer: I like [maths]. It's fun.

translationRu.text: Какой у тебя пока любимый предмет?

text: Are you okay? You look a bit lost. Do you need a hand?
rephrase: Are you okay? Do you need help?
gist: Do you need help?
distractors: Did you lose your hand?
Are you going home now?
sampleAnswer: Yes, please. I can't find my classroom.

translationRu.text: Ты в порядке? Ты как будто потерялась. Тебе помочь?
translationRu.sampleAnswer: Да, пожалуйста. Я не могу найти свой класс.

text: Can you say that again, a bit louder? I didn't quite catch it.
rephrase: Please say that again, louder. I didn't hear you.
gist: Please say it again, louder.
distractors: Please stop talking.
Please write it down.
sampleAnswer: Sorry! I'm still learning English. I said [your words].

translationRu.text: Можешь повторить чуть громче? Я не расслышала.
translationRu.sampleAnswer: Извините! Я еще учу английский. Я сказала [твои слова].

text: Have you got a lunch order today, or did you bring lunch from home?
rephrase: Did you order lunch at school, or bring lunch from home?
gist: Did you order lunch or bring it from home?
distractors: Do you want to cook lunch?
What time is lunch?

phrases.meaning: lunch you order from the school canteen

sampleAnswer: I brought lunch from home.

translationRu.text: Ты заказала обед сегодня или принесла из дома?

text: We've got assembly after recess, so line up at the door, please.
rephrase: We have a school meeting after the break. Please stand in a line at the door.
gist: Line up at the door for assembly.
distractors: Sit at your desk after recess.
Go home after assembly.

phrases.meaning: a meeting of the whole school

sampleAnswer: Okay! Can I stand next to you?

translationRu.text: После перемены общешкольное собрание, встаньте в линию у двери, пожалуйста.
translationRu.sampleAnswer: Хорошо! Можно мне встать рядом с тобой?

text: Is someone picking you up this arvo, or are you going to after-school care?
rephrase: Is someone coming to get you this afternoon, or are you staying at after-school care?
gist: Who is taking you home this afternoon?
distractors: Do you want to go to the park this afternoon?
Do you like your teacher?

phrases.meaning: a place where kids stay after school

sampleAnswer: My [mum] is picking me up.

translationRu.text: Тебя кто-то заберет после обеда или ты идешь на продленку?
